name: Whole Lotta Love
reference: Whole Lotta Love (92 BPM, E): Led Zeppelin, Led Zeppelin II (1969; Olympic London and A&M, April 1969, prod. Jimmy Page, mixed by Eddie Kramer)
rig: 1959 Les Paul Standard (bought from Joe Walsh in early 1969, 'used to record Zeppelin II') -> on the solo a wah held in one position ('a depressed wah-wah pedal, as on Communication Breakdown') -> Page (Total Guitar, 2020): 'I was using the Super Beatle amps with the [Rickenbacker] Transonic cabinets... That's exactly what's on Whole Lotta Love' (a solid-state Vox; J.J. Blair's multitrack analysis agrees; John Paul Jones: 'a really small amplifier', close-miked). Middle section: theremin, the Les Paul, backwards echo and console 'knob twiddling'.
notes: APPROXIMATION: the amp Page names, a Vox Super Beatle into Rickenbacker Transonic cabs, has no capture in the catalog. A 1969 Marshall JMP Super Lead full rig stands in (Songfacts says a 100 W Plexi; Marshalls reached Page around March 1969, groundguitar). Les Paul humbuckers, so no pre-EQ. For the solo: SW6 WAH, then park EXP A toe-forward (the fixed wah). SW8 BOOST = TS9 clean push (not on the record); SW9 = an eighth-note echo at 92 BPM for the middle section (the record's backwards echo can't be played live); 480L Large Wood Room for Olympic's room. Not compared by ear with a Super Beatle. Levelled offline with rigsim --exact to -14 LUFS (experiments D28).

left.label: Ibanez TS9 clean push, D0 T6 L10 (lead boost, not on the record)
1969 Marshall JMP Super Lead 100 W (full rig; stands in for the Vox Super Beatle Page named)
Eighth-note echo 326 ms at 92 BPM (the middle section's echo, approximated)
Lexicon 480L Large Wood Room (Olympic Studio One's live room)
